policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the substantival expression with the article as 'the wicked' ('the wickedness of the wicked'), distinguishing the qere/base from the anarthrous ketiv.
ASV has the plural 'all his sins,' distinguishing qere/base חטאתיו from the singular ketiv חטאתו.
ASV renders 'None of his righteous deeds,' whose plural distinguishes qere/base צדקתיו from singular ketiv צדקתו.
ASV's present-tense 'turneth away,' coordinated with 'considereth,' distinguishes ketiv וישוב from qere/base וישב.
